title: Risotto al Nero di Seppia
subtitle: Venetian squid ink risotto
excerpt: Risotto al nero di seppia is a Venetian rice dish coloured jet black with squid ink and flavoured with squid, white wine, and a little tomato. The ink gives the risotto a briny, faintly metallic depth that is distinct from anything else in Italian cooking. It is dramatic on the plate and completely delicious.
sourceNotes: Risotto al nero di seppia is a classic Venetian dish from the lagoon, where cuttlefish and squid are abundant. The dish appears in Venetian cookery records from the nineteenth century. The ink is traditionally squeezed fresh from the ink sac, but ready-prepared sachets of squid ink are widely available and produce an identical result.

content.text: Squid ink risotto requires the soffritto (the base of onion and garlic in olive oil) to be cooked very gently before anything else goes in. The ink is added with the wine, not at the end, so it has time to cook into the rice. Do not add butter or Parmesan at the finish: the dish is dairy-free by tradition.

items.prepNote: cleaned, body cut into rings, tentacles left whole

content.text: Warm {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over a low heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 10 minutes until completely soft but not coloured. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 2 minutes more.

Add {{carnaroli-rice}} of rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are coated and slightly translucent at the edges. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} of white wine. Add {{squid-ink}} sachets of squid ink and stir well. The rice will turn black immediately. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tomato and stir.

Add {{chicken-stock}} hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Continue for about 18 minutes until the rice is al dente and has a flowing, creamy consistency. Season with {{salt-table}} salt.

Meanwhile, heat a little olive oil in a separate frying pan over a high heat. Quickly fry {{squid}} squid for 2 minutes until just firm. Season. Arrange on top of the risotto to serve. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over if using.

items.symptom: The risotto is stiff rather than flowing
items.cause: Not enough stock was used, or the risotto was left to rest too long before serving.
items.fix: Risotto al nero should be very loose (all'onda -- wavy). Add a final ladleful of warm stock and stir vigorously before plating. Serve the moment it is done.

content.text: Risotto al nero di seppia is one of the defining dishes of Venice. The Venetian lagoon has been rich in cuttlefish and squid for centuries, and the ink has been used in cooking there longer than anywhere else in Italy. The dish is almost always served without cheese: Parmesan on fish dishes is considered a serious error in Venice. It appears on the menus of simple trattorie and high-end restaurants alike.
